title: reAlpha (NASDAQ: AIRE) Appoints Thomas Kutzman to Lead Brokerage Division as CEO of reAlpha Realty
summary: reAlpha appoints Thomas Kutzman as CEO of reAlpha Realty, supporting national brokerage growth and integration of Prevu’s platform
body_text: Seasoned real estate technology leader to oversee integration of Prevu and drive reAlpha’s national brokerage expansion DUBLIN, OH – Dec. 03, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - reAlpha Tech Corp. (Nasdaq: AIRE) (“reAlpha” or the “Company”), an AI-powered real estate technology company, today announced the appointment of Thomas Kutzman as Chief Executive Officer of reAlpha Realty, the Company’s real estate brokerage division. Kutzman joined reAlpha Realty as part of the Company’s acquisition of Prevu, Inc. (“Prevu”) in November 2025. As co-founder of Prevu, he helped build an innovative digital homebuying platform, operating across 12 states and Washington, D.C. Under his leadership, Prevu was named to the 2022 Inc. 5000 list of the fastest-growing private companies in America and became known for its technology-forward, transparent, and consumer-centric brokerage model. “Thomas has already demonstrated what it takes to scale a modern, technology-enabled brokerage,” said Mike Logozzo, Chief Executive Officer of reAlpha. “His experience building Prevu and delivering a differentiated consumer experience makes him the right leader to guide reAlpha Realty as we integrate the Prevu platform and expand our brokerage footprint across key markets.” As CEO of reAlpha Realty, Kutzman will lead the strategic development and national expansion of the Company’s real estate business. His responsibilities include shaping the long-term vision for reAlpha’s brokerage platform, strengthening alignment with the Company’s mortgage and title operations, and advancing a unified model that improves efficiency, customer experience, and agent productivity across key markets. He will oversee the integration of Prevu’s technology and operational capabilities into reAlpha’s real estate ecosystem while building the foundation for a scaled, technology-driven brokerage that supports reAlpha’s multi-service growth plan. “Stepping into this role is a natural extension of the work we began at Prevu,” said Thomas Kutzman, Chief Executive Officer of reAlpha Realty. “reAlpha’s integrated approach is creating a better, more connected homebuying experience. I am excited to lead reAlpha Realty as we expand our brokerage capabilities and deliver greater value to the customers and agents we serve.” Kutzman will report directly to Logozzo and join the Company’s executive leadership team. About reAlpha Tech Corp. reAlpha Tech Corp. (Nasdaq: AIRE) is an AI-powered real estate technology company that aims to transform the multi-trillion-dollar U.S. real estate services market. reAlpha is developing an end-to-end platform that streamlines real estate transactions through integrated brokerage, mortgage, and title services. With a strategic, acquisition-driven growth model and proprietary AI infrastructure, reAlpha is building a vertically integrated ecosystem designed to deliver a simpler, smarter, and more affordable path to homeownership. For more information, visit www.realpha.com . title: Portable WiFi for Family Holidays and Multi-Device Households
summary: Discover how a dedicated travel hotspot can simplify family trips across Europe. Enjoy flexible data plans, connect up to 16 devices and stay secure wherever you go.
body_text: Planning a family getaway is always exciting, but keeping everyone connected while on the move can quickly become a major headache. Whether it's keeping younger children entertained with streaming shows during long motorway drives, using live maps to navigate unfamiliar city streets, or ensuring parents can stay on top of work emails, reliable internet is no longer a luxury – it's a necessity. Relying on public hotspots or individual roaming packages often means high costs and sluggish performance. Investing in a dedicated portable WiFi device offers a dependable solution to keep every smartphone, tablet, and laptop securely online, no matter where your European adventure takes you. A quality portable WiFi device is essentially a compact wireless router that fits in your pocket. It creates a private internet connection using cellular data, establishing a secure local network just for your family. When travelling with multiple gadgets – from games consoles to e-readers – a single dedicated hotspot means everyone can enjoy high-speed data simultaneously. This comprehensive guide explores why a portable WiFi device is a game-changer for family travel, and how modern solutions can keep your entire group seamlessly connected throughout your trip. Why Is Portable WiFi Indispensable for Modern Family Travel? Streaming entertainment, real-time GPS navigation, and instant messaging can quickly overwhelm a smartphone's personal hotspot, draining its battery and causing overheating. Portable WiFi devices are specifically engineered to handle significant data traffic from multiple users at once, delivering a far more stable and reliable connection than typical phone tethering. Security is another critical factor when travelling abroad. Public networks in airports, cafés, and hotels are often unencrypted, leaving your personal data – such as banking details, booking confirmations, and private messages – exposed to potential cyber risks. With your own portable WiFi device, you create a password-protected network that uses the latest encryption standards, keeping your family's digital life safe. Additionally, a dedicated hotspot helps families avoid unexpected roaming charges. Instead of purchasing separate international passes or local SIM cards for each member, a single device provides WiFi for multiple devices under one unified, easy-to-manage data plan – a much more economical approach for European trips that may span several countries. Core Benefits: Designed for Multiple Family Devices The practical advantages of purpose-built hardware become clear when compared to public networks or smartphone hotspots, especially when managing the diverse digital needs of a large family on the move. The standout benefits include: Simultaneous Connections for the Whole Household: Premium portable WiFi devices support between 10 and 16 concurrent connections. This means children can stream cartoons on their tablets, teenagers can play online games, and parents can join video conferences – all without buffering or dropouts. All-Day Battery Life for Full Excursions: Specialised travel hotspots come with high-capacity internal batteries that deliver continuous operation for 11 to 15 hours on a single charge. This removes the worry of draining a parent's phone battery through tethering during a long day of sightseeing. Fair Bandwidth Distribution: Unlike phones that prioritise their own background tasks, dedicated travel routers allocate data evenly across all connected devices, ensuring no single user hogs the connection. Superior Signal Stability on the Move: These devices are equipped with advanced internal antennas that are more effective at locking onto weak cellular signals than standard smartphones. This provides a more consistent connection for the family inside moving vehicles, trains, or even in remote holiday cottages across the European countryside. Top Portable WiFi Picks for European Family Travel Choosing the right model for your family means balancing speed, connection capacity, and ease of use. Two standout options from GlocalMe are specifically tailored to meet the demands of modern group travel across Europe. For Maximum Performance: GlocalMe Numen Air For families who demand top-tier speed, the Numen Air is a premium choice. This powerful device supports global 5G networks, delivering ultra-fast internet with minimal latency – perfect for 4K streaming, high-quality video calls, or uploading holiday photos in seconds. Connection Capacity: Supports up to 16 devices at once, making it simple to share WiFi for multiple devices including laptops, tablets, and smart speakers. Battery & Power: Features a substantial 5,400mAh battery that provides up to 11 hours of continuous 5G use (or 15 hours on 4G), and can even serve as a reverse-charging power bank for your phone – a lifesaver during long train journeys across Europe. User Interface: Equipped with a clear 2.4-inch colour touchscreen, allowing you to monitor data usage and signal strength at a glance. For Smart, Adaptive Travel: GlocalMe MeowGo G40 Pro If portability and intelligent network switching are your priorities, the MeowGo G40 Pro is a highly efficient companion. Powered by AI HyperConn technology, this 4G+ mobile hotspot constantly analyses and optimises your connection, automatically selecting the best-performing network from hundreds of carriers across Europe and beyond. Connection Capacity: Securely connects up to 10 smart devices at once – ideal for a standard family trip. Optimised Speeds: Delivers fast 4G+ performance with download speeds reaching up to 390 Mbps. Compact Design: Features an ultra-slim, lightweight body with a vibrant touch display, slipping easily into a pocket or daypack for city exploration. Flexible Data Plans and Extensive Carrier Support One of the greatest advantages of modern travel hotspots is the flexibility they offer in data management. These devices do not lock you into expensive annual contracts; instead, they provide pay-as-you-go structures that suit different travel patterns. Through the GlocalMe Data Store, travellers can choose from local data packs, regional bundles (ideal for multi-country European tours), or comprehensive global plans. These devices are fully compatible with major local carriers across more than 200 countries and regions. The built-in systems automatically connect to the strongest local network whenever you arrive – whether you're in a bustling capital like Paris, a coastal town in Spain, or a Alpine village in Switzerland – ensuring consistent, fast service without excessive international roaming fees. Practical Tips for Managing Portable WiFi with Multiple Family Devices To get the most out of your hotspot during family trips, here are some tried-and-tested recommendations: Limit background data usage: Phones and tablets often auto-update apps, back up photos, and sync cloud data once connected to WiFi. To avoid burning through your travel allowance too quickly, enable "Low Data Mode" or temporarily turn off automatic updates and background syncing for the duration of your trip. Position for optimal coverage: When inside a car, hotel room, or holiday rental, place the hotspot in a central, elevated spot – such as on a dashboard or a table near a window. This helps distribute a strong WiFi signal evenly to every device without interference from walls or furniture. Pre-download heavy content: Before you set off, download large movie files, offline maps, and heavy games onto kids' devices while connected to your home or airport WiFi. This saves your precious high-speed data for essential tasks like navigation and work calls. Keep Your Family Connected Across Europe and Beyond A stable internet connection is key to making your family travels smooth, safe, and enjoyable. By investing in a dedicated portable WiFi device, you eliminate the stress of staying connected, avoid the security pitfalls of public networks, and bypass the exorbitant costs of individual roaming plans. Whether you choose the Numen Air's blazing 5G performance or the MeowGo G40 Pro's smart, AI-driven connectivity, these devices ensure your family stays safely online wherever your European journey leads. Flexible data options are available now on the official GlocalMe shop – explore them and pick the perfect setup for your next holiday. Frequently Asked Questions Does portable WiFi actually work well? Yes, a dedicated portable WiFi device works very effectively. It uses powerful internal antennas to pull in mobile data signals from nearby network towers, then broadcasts a secure, password-protected local network – just like your home broadband. This provides a stable, high-speed connection for multiple people to browse, navigate, and stream simultaneously while travelling. How much does portable WiFi cost per month? The monthly cost depends entirely on your travel habits, as modern portable WiFi devices typically offer flexible, contract-free pay-as-you-go options. Rather than a fixed monthly subscription, you can purchase regional weekly bundles or global packages directly through the companion app. This transparent model keeps travel costs under control by charging you only for the data your family actually uses. Are portable WiFi devices worth the investment? Absolutely – especially for families who travel with multiple smartphones, tablets, and laptops. A dedicated hotspot means you avoid expensive international roaming fees on each individual line, and you keep your personal data away from the security risks of public networks at airports or hotels. A reliable source of WiFi for multiple devices keeps the kids entertained and lets parents explore confidently, without worrying about network dropouts.

title: Get more flexible, accessible employee drug testing with oral fluid drug tests
summary: Simplify employee drug screening with oral fluid testing. Oral fluid drug testing offers flexible collections, nationwide access, streamlined HR workflows, and more.
body_text: Workplace drug testing continues to evolve as employers look for approaches that align with today’s regulatory landscape, a better employee experience, operational realities, administrative complexities, and safer, more productive environments. Oral fluid testing has emerged as an excellent alternative to traditional methodologies, offering a unique balance of efficiency, accuracy, and accessibility. Recent regulatory shifts and technological advancements have brought oral fluid drug testing to the forefront of workplace safety strategies, as the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Department of Transportation (DOT) updated their regulations to allow oral fluid testing in federally regulated programs. These milestones highlight a broader industry trend toward more flexible, private, and efficient screening methods that support both organizational goals and employee well-being. Here’s how oral fluid drug testing helps support these goals. Four advantages of oral fluid testing 1. Simplifies and streamlines the process for operational efficiency Oral fluid testing simplifies and streamlines specimen collection compared to urine testing since the process typically takes just a few minutes and requires minimal setup. This helps reduce delays, downtime for staff, and overall administrative burden. 2. Increases access for your employees Because collections involve placing a swab in the mouth, testing can take place in a wider range of environments without the need for specialized facilities. This operational flexibility supports on-site testing, remote locations, and time-sensitive scenarios like post-accident or reasonable suspicion testing. 3. Enables direct observation and a more private experience Another key benefit of oral fluid testing is that direct observation is built into the process, which creates a more respectful and less invasive experience for employees compared to traditional observed urine collections. Because collections are directly observed and conducted under controlled conditions, oral fluid testing makes specimen tampering, adulteration, or substitution extremely difficult. This helps: Improve confidence in results Reduce the need for additional oversight or repeat collections Protect the integrity of your entire workplace drug testing program The direct observation process also simplifies logistics. Gender-neutral collection protocols help eliminate the need to match donors and collectors, and fewer environmental requirements reduce variability across collection sites, which streamlines scheduling and staffing for testing. 4. Provides a better lens into recent drug use From a clinical and safety perspective, oral fluid testing excels at detecting very recent drug use. The test screens for the parent psychoactive drug, which remains in the system for a short period, typically within hours to a day, depending on the substance. This short detection window provides employers with relevant insights to identify active impairment or recent use, which aligns closely with real-time workplace needs for safety-sensitive roles in post-accident or reasonable suspicion scenarios. While urine testing detects drug metabolites over a longer period, oral fluid testing provides immediate insight into recent consumption. At the same time, the shorter detection window reflects broader shifts in workplace policy. With changing marijuana laws across states, many employers seek approaches that distinguish between past use and recent consumption. To achieve this, oral fluid testing uses cutoff levels that are significantly lower than urine testing levels. Advanced analytical capabilities reliably detect these lower concentrations, supporting a highly accurate and compliant screening process that meets rigorous quality standards. Achieving a more streamlined drug testing and billing experience Implementing an effective drug testing program requires a partner who understands the operational demands of modern businesses. Labcorp brings over two decades of experience to oral fluid testing and now offers a rapid oral fluid test at select patient service centers (PSCs). This experience helps you navigate evolving regulatory compliance, manage risk, and design testing programs that align with your specific safety goals. To make the testing process as seamless as possible, we offer a unique bundled service model for our rapid oral fluid test. This includes: A point-of-care oral fluid test for collection Shipping to the laboratory for non-negative results Laboratory confirmation testing on the same device Many point-of-care oral fluid tests require a separate, second collection if a sample requires confirmation testing. By conducting laboratory confirmation testing on the same device, we eliminate the second step, saving time and reducing stress for employees. Employers receive this comprehensive service for a single flat fee, which simplifies budgeting, billing, and administrative tracking across the organization in a predictable structure. It allows you to spend less time coordinating logistics and reconciling invoices and more time focusing on broader workforce priorities. This streamlined approach uses the FDA-cleared OralTox 10-panel rapid oral fluid drug test. This panel screens for 10 of the most commonly tested drug classes, including: Amphetamine Barbiturates Benzodiazepines Cocaine Methamphetamine Marijuana Methadone Opiates Oxycodone Phencyclidine The panel is customizable and helps employers maintain comprehensive screening standards without needing multiple separate tests. Expanding access and efficiency with Labcorp As oral fluid testing gains traction, how it’s delivered becomes just as important as the method itself. Access, consistency, and integration into existing workflows all shape how well a program performs. A broader network of collection sites plays a key role in accessibility. With more than 1,100 patient service centers (PSCs) nationwide that offer rapid oral fluid collections, testing can take place closer to where employees live and work. The ability to collect without a compliant restroom will soon expand our footprint even further, with plans to open additional PSCs for rapid oral fluid testing in the future, increasing convenience for both employers and employees. This expanded access can help reduce travel time, limit disruptions to the workday, and support faster turnaround on testing events. Supporting employees while maintaining workplace safety program integrity Drug testing programs operate at the intersection of safety, compliance, and employee experience. Oral fluid testing can support all three when implemented thoughtfully, with approaches that are easier to administer, better aligned with real-time detection, and adaptable to changing regulations. A less invasive collection process helps preserve dignity during testing events. Shorter appointment times and more accessible locations reduce disruption to the workday and fewer repeat collections help simplify the overall experience. At the same time, direct observation and reduced adulteration risk help reinforce program integrity. Employers can maintain confidence in results while offering a process that feels more balanced for employees. The work you do to maintain a safe, productive, and supportive workplace is vital to your organization's success. Partnering with an experienced provider for oral fluid drug testing helps you protect your workforce while respecting their privacy and time. Through reliable data, predictable pricing, and nationwide access, we support your commitment to advancing workplace health and safety as you build a stronger, more resilient organization. Consult with us to maximize the effectiveness of your program as you navigate this transition. Together, we can enhance your drug testing program and contribute to safer, more productive workplaces. title: 2Q2026 ING press release
body_text: Profit before tax of €2,919 million, up 23% year-on-year and 29% quarter-on-quarter Mobile primary customer base expands by 377,000 in the quarter, demonstrating continued commercial momentum €15.2 billion of net core lending growth and €15.9 billion of net core deposit inflows Fee income of €1,278 million, up 14% year-on-year and 3% higher quarter-on-quarter Return on tangible equity 17.0% in 2Q2026 and 14.5% on a four-quarter rolling basis; CET1 ratio 13.1% ING will pay an interim cash dividend of €0.40 per ordinary share Upgraded 2026 and 2027 outlook for fees and total income, with ROTE now expected at >15% and >16%, respectively CEO statement “ING has had an excellent second quarter of 2026, with strong results across all business lines as more customers did more business with us,” said Steven van Rijswijk, CEO of ING. “These results reflect the continued progress we are making and show that we are successfully supporting our clients and customers during this period of ongoing uncertainty. “During the quarter, more customers have chosen to bank with ING, with our mobile primary customer base growing by 377,000, with strong contributions from the Netherlands, Germany and Spain. Total income was 10% higher and the net result has increased 16% year-on-year, supported by growth in both interest and fee income, reflecting our strong commercial momentum across the franchise. “In Retail Banking, lending has grown by €12.1 billion, or 9% on an annualised basis. We have helped more people finance their homes, leading to a €7.1 billion growth in mortgages, especially in the Netherlands, Germany, Italy and Australia. We have also extended more loans to our Business Banking clients, resulting in lending growth of €4.2 billion. And customers have continued to entrust more of their savings to us, supported by successful deposit gathering campaigns across several markets and resulting in €16.7 billion Retail deposits growth, or 10% on an annualised basis. "Retail fee income has grown by 16% year-on-year, benefiting from our growing customer base and increased customer activity. We also continued to help more customers invest for their future. The number of active investment product customers has increased by 110,000 in the quarter, with strong growth in Germany in particular, and total assets under management have grown 27% year on year to €322 billion, partially supported by the full consolidation of Polish asset manager TFI, after acquiring the remaining stake. To further accelerate our growth in Private Banking, we have announced a strategic investment in leading Spanish wealth manager Singular Bank, which will strengthen our position in one of Europe’s largest wealth markets. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. “In Wholesale Banking, we have seen strong performance across Lending, Daily Banking & Trade Finance, and Financial Markets. Quarterly lending growth was €3 billion, or 6% on an annualised basis, mainly driven by consistent demand for financing from our clients as well as growth in Transaction Services. We also improved capital efficiency, reducing risk-weighted assets despite continued lending growth. Wholesale Banking fee income has increased 11% year-on-year, as we continue to support more clients in their investment needs. “Expenses increased, mainly reflecting wage inflation and continued investments to support business growth, including marketing expenses. Risk costs have remained below the through-the-cycle average at 15 basis points of average customer lending. Return on tangible equity was 17.0% in the second quarter, bringing the four-quarter rolling average to 14.5%. Our CET1 ratio was 13.1%, which includes the €1.0 billion RWA relief from another significant risk-transfer (SRT) transaction completed during the quarter. “As we continue to support our clients in their transition to a more sustainable future, we financed €86.5 billion in sustainable volume mobilised in the first half of 2026. Furthermore, we helped more customers finance energy-efficient homes and provided more financing for home renovations aimed at improving energy efficiency. “Looking ahead, we remain well positioned to support our customers and clients, as we build on our strong momentum and disciplined strategic execution. We thank our employees for their dedication and contribution to these results.” More details in the 2Q2026 press release download . Analyst call on 30 July 2Q2026 ING analyst call | replay Note for editors For further information on ING, please visit www.ing.com . Frequent news updates can be found in the Newsroom . Photos of ING operations, buildings and its executives are available for download at Flickr . ING profile ING is a global financial institution with a strong European base, offering banking services through its operating company ING Bank. The purpose of ING Bank is: empowering people to stay a step ahead in life and in business. ING Bank’s more than 60,000 employees offer retail and wholesale banking services to customers in over 100 countries. ING Group shares are listed on the exchanges of Amsterdam (INGA NA, INGA.AS), Brussels and on the New York Stock Exchange (ADRs: ING US, ING.N). ING aims to put sustainability at the heart of what we do. Our policies and actions are assessed by independent research and ratings providers, which give updates on them annually. title: Cosmic Rundown: GPT-5.6 Math Breakthroughs, LG Silent Installs, and Stack Overflow's AI Decline
summary: GPT-5.6 closes 30-year math gap, LG monitors install software without consent, Stack Overflow activity drops as AI takes over developer questions, plus EU fashion waste ban and exoplanet news.
body_text: GPT-5.6 and a 30-Year Math Problem A Reddit post claims GPT-5.6 used a prompt to close a long-standing gap in convex optimization theory. The Hacker News discussion is picking apart the claim, with mathematicians weighing in on whether this represents genuine progress or clever pattern matching. Separately, a comparison of Fable 5 vs. GPT-5.6 Sol on an NP-Hard Problem explores whether the new directive actually helps with complex reasoning tasks. The HN thread digs into benchmarking methodology. LG Monitors Install Software Without Asking LG monitors are silently installing software through Windows Update without user consent. The software reportedly includes OnScreen Control and other utilities that users never requested. The Hacker News discussion is extensive, with users debating whether hardware manufacturers should have this level of access to push software installs. Several commenters noted they discovered unexpected LG processes running on their machines. For teams managing content infrastructure, unexpected software installs are a reminder why control over your stack matters. A headless CMS like Cosmic keeps your content layer clean and predictable. What AI Did to Stack Overflow A Stack Exchange query visualization shows the dramatic decline in Stack Overflow activity since AI coding assistants became mainstream. The graph tells a clear story about how developers now get answers. The HN thread debates whether this is a net positive (faster answers) or net negative (less community knowledge being created). Some argue the drop reflects question quality improving as trivial questions go to AI first. EU Bans Destroying Unsold Clothes The EU ban on destroying unsold clothes and shoes is now in effect. The regulation targets fast fashion waste by requiring brands to find alternatives to destruction. The discussion explores implementation challenges and whether this will shift manufacturing behavior or just offshoring of destruction. First Atmosphere on an Earth-Like Exoplanet Astronomers detected the first atmosphere on an Earth-like planet in a habitable zone. The James Webb Space Telescope identified the atmospheric signature on a planet orbiting a distant star. The HN conversation clarifies what "Earth-like" and "habitable zone" actually mean in this context. An atmosphere alone doesn't indicate life, but it's a meaningful step in exoplanet research. Quick Hits Regressive JPEGs. A project called Regressive JPEGs explores what happens when you intentionally degrade JPEG compression in creative ways. The discussion goes deep on image encoding theory. TP-Link cameras leaked GPS for 6 years. Research reveals that TP-Link Kasa cameras broadcast home GPS coordinates via unauthenticated UDP. The thread discusses IoT security practices. The Zilog Z80 turns 50. A retrospective on the Z80 celebrates five decades of the processor that powered countless early computers. The nostalgia runs deep in the comments. SQLite learnings. Julia Evans shares practical lessons about running SQLite in production. The discussion adds deployment tips from experienced users. Gleam on Tangled. The Gleam programming language joined Tangled , a new decentralized code hosting platform. The HN thread discusses alternatives to centralized Git hosting. Claude Code Mac setup guide. A step-by-step guide for setting up a spare Mac for Claude Code to control is making the rounds. The comments share additional configuration tips. title: Go behind the scenes of Lollapalooza with an exclusive fan experience
summary: Lollapalooza fans are going beyond the crowd in 2026, with an exclusive Airbnb Experience offering rare backstage access to the festival.
body_text: This year, Airbnb is taking fans behind-the-scenes at Lollapalooza. Through an exclusive Airbnb Experience , guests can go backstage with Tim Sweetwood—a pioneering force in the live music world and the founder behind Shaky Knees Music Festival, Oceans Calling, Country Calling, Boardwalk Rock, Sea.Hear.Now, and more—for rare access to the parts of the festival most fans only dream about, from artist compounds and production zones to the hidden corners that make the magic happen. Fans can also catch live sets at the new Airbnb stage, with performances from fan-favorite artists all weekend long. Out-of-state travelers are flocking to Chicago this Lollapalooza Lollapalooza is bringing more visitors to Chicago this year, with fans already planning their trips for the festival weekend, and the demand has translated into real impact for the local community: Out-of-state travelers are making a weekend of it, with their searches up almost 20%.1 Gen Z is showing strong interest with searches up 15%.2 Chicago hosts collectively earned over $6.4 million during last year’s festival weekend alone.3 “Live music has become one of the biggest drivers of travel today, and Lollapalooza is a perfect example, bringing fans from across the country and around the world to Chicago every summer. Through our global partnership, we’re giving guests access to something truly special: exclusive backstage experiences at one of the world’s most iconic festivals, paired with everything they need to make their time in the city just as memorable as the music.” Juan David Borrero, Global Head of Partnerships and Business Development at Airbnb With listings still available across the city, including in neighborhoods well outside Chicago’s traditional hotel corridors, there’s still time to find the perfect home base for the weekend. In fact, over 70 percent of census tracts in Chicago are home to Airbnb listings but not hotels, expanding opportunities to earn for more residents across the city. 3 Bed/2 Bath by United Center w/ Private Parking Architect-Designed 3BR Oak Park Flat Cozy and Spacious! Logan Square Apartment Sloth Apt • King Bed • Parking • Walk 2 Blue Line 3BD | 2 Ensuites | Sleeps 8 | Near Sox & McCormick 1 / 5 Guests can explore Chicago beyond the festival grounds during Lollapalooza weekend When the music stops, the fun doesn’t have to. Between sets and before the next act, Airbnb Experiences and Services give festival-goers the perfect way to fill their downtime and go deeper into everything Chicago has to offer. Guests can recharge with an authentic Thai massage or gather the crew for a private dinner at their Airbnb with Chef Pasquale , a personal chef with 21 years of experience serving up authentic Italian cooking. And when they’re ready to explore, there’s no shortage of ways to make the most of the city: Enjoy Spanish Tapas and Live Flamenco : Guests will savor four Spanish tapas crafted by a Michelin Star restaurant chef, then watch and join a live flamenco performance. Chicago’s Sweetest Sights: Donuts, Coffee and More : This experience takes guests through the city’s food culture, hitting its best donut stops, including Doughnut Vault, plus other popular spots such as Do-Rite. Make Mexican Mole Sauce from Scratch : Guests will learn ancestral smoking techniques and prepare a traditional family mole recipe, then sit down to enjoy it. Walkin’ With Colin Chicago Tour du Jour : This walking tour uncovers the history, art, and iconic architecture of The Loop, ending at Millennium Park. Paint Your Own Street Art at Studio WIP : Guests will get hands-on with local street artists at this Uptown studio and leave with a finished canvas.
